statement: There exists a real number x with x·x = 0. Research.answer is a real number defined by classical choice of a witness to this existence statement. Research.answer_correct states that this chosen real number satisfies Research.answer·Research.answer = 0. Real arithmetic consequently forces the chosen value to be 0; the defining construction selects a witness rather than explicitly returning the numeral 0.

targets.name: Research.answer._proof_1
targets.statement: There exists x ∈ ℝ such that x·x = 0. There are no additional hypotheses or free parameters. Multiplication and 0 are real multiplication and real zero.

targets.name: Research.answer_correct
targets.statement: For the real number Research.answer defined by classical choice from Research.answer._proof_1, Research.answer·Research.answer = 0. There are no additional hypotheses, free parameters, or quantified variables.

constructions.name: Research.answer
constructions.description: A real number defined as Classical.choose applied to Research.answer._proof_1: it selects a witness x of ∃ x ∈ ℝ, x·x = 0. It has no arguments or implicit parameters. Its defining body is classical witness selection; Research.answer_correct states that the selected witness satisfies the equation. Since the only real number whose square is zero is zero, its value is necessarily 0.

assumptions: Both target statements are closed: neither has any explicit or implicit hypothesis, free parameter, or numerical bound.
The existential variable x has domain ℝ, as identified by the supplied real multiplication and zero instances. All displayed products and zeros are in ℝ.
The construction uses classical choice on the existence theorem Research.answer._proof_1.
